full_judgment:
A.K.M. Asaduzzaman, J. These 2(two) revisions arising out of the same judgment and order dated 18.5.2010 passed by the learned Sessions Judge, Chapai Nawabgonj in Criminal Misc. Case No. 154 of 2010 arising out of G.R. Case No.365 of 2008 (Shib) corresponding to Shibgonj P.S. Case No.38 dated 25.10.2008 under section 7(1),7(2),8,9 (1),12 of the Santras Birodhi Ain( Amended in 2009) granting bail to the petitioner as well as stayed the order of bail by the order dated 23.6.2010 and as such heard together and disposed of by a single judgment. 

 Facts relevant for disposal of the rule are that on 25.10.2008 at 01.30 AM on the basis of secret information Md. Abul Kalam Azad, officer-in-charge along with his police personal made campaign in the house of one Ekramul Huq, son of Entaz Ali of village- Biswanathpur, Kansat Union under Shibgonj Police Station; that they gheraoed the said house and arrested JMB Members Rafiul and Hazrat Ali; that at that time noticing the presence of the police other JMB members and Ekram, owner of the house, fled away; that they searched the place of occurrence and seized various alamats according to rules; that thereafter the informant lodged the FIR with the Shibgonj Police Station against 6(six) accused and other unknown accuseds and hence the case. 

 The case was duly been investigated by the police, who submitted a charge sheet on 27.9.09 under sections 7(1), 7(2), 8,9(1), 12 of the Santras Birodhi Ain (Amended in 2009) against the accused petitioner and others. During investigation one 

 Being aggrieved there against the petitioner Md. Yousuf Ali filed a Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.154 of 2010 before the Court of Sessions Judge, Chapai Nawabgonj on 5.5.2010. By the order dated 18.5.2010 the learned Sessions judge granted bail to the petitioner and on that date the learned Public Prosecutor appearing for the State filed an application for staying the operation of the impugned judgment and the order dated 18.5.10 with a disclosure that he has got instruction to file An appeal before the Hon’ble High Court Division against the said order. Accordingly the learned Sessions Judge by the order dated 23.6.10 stayed the order dated 18.05.10. Thus against the order dated 23.6.10 the petitioner Md. Yousuf Ali preferred Criminal Revision No.1256 of 2010 and against the order dated 18.5.2010 Criminal Revision No.1306 of 2010 was filed by the State. Accordingly these 2(two) rules issued by the Hon’ble High Court Division are being heard and disposed of by this judgment. 

 Mr. Md. Zahanagir Alam, the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner Md. Yousuf Ali in Criminal Revision No.1256 of 2010 on drawing our attention to the order dated 18.5.10 submits that the learned Sessions Judge after correct assessment of the factual aspect of the case and considering the submission of the accused petitioner found that the petitioner is fully innocent and he is not a member of the JMB and the confessing accused Md. Rafiqul Islam alias Jubayer alias Rashel alias Jasim did not implicate the accused petitioner with the occurrence and considering the detention period from 5.1.10 he allowed the prayer of the petitioner and granted him bail correctly and there is nothing to interfere in the said judgment and accordingly  Criminal Revision filed by the State is required to be discharged and the order of stay granted by the Sessions Judge subsequently by the order dated 23.6.10 may be set aside and the petitioner may be allowed to go on bail. The learned Assistant Attorney General appearing for the 

 State in both the rules although tried to make out a case that the learned Sessions Judge while granting bail was not applying his judgment mind and granted bail arbitrarily but since nowhere the petitioner Md. Yousuf Ali was being mentioned to have connected with the JMB, and the confessing accused since did not mention the name of the petitioner, found it difficult to oppose the bail of the petitioner Md. Yousuf Ali.
